problem: Existing VLN simulators depend on expensive 3D scans, meshes and sparse pre-defined viewpoint graphs, so new large environments are hard to build. 3DGS built from forward-facing robot traversal data has floor artifacts (floaters, blur) and has no mesh for collision or traversability checking.
motivation: Scalable, cheap simulators are needed to evaluate zero-shot LLM navigators in varied, large public spaces beyond residential scans. Robot traversal image sequences are cheap, but sparse floor observations and the lack of a mesh make them unsuitable as navigable simulators without new methods.
key_idea: Build a navigable simulator from image sequences with submap-wise Gaussian Splatting, where the floor is rendered by a background spherical-harmonics MLP instead of Gaussians, and derive a topological graph by checking traversability directly on rendered alpha and normal maps.
insight: Replacing the floor with a low-frequency background model plus a floor suppression loss removes floor artifacts, and a mesh-free graph can be built from rendered views. Ablation (Table 2): masking alone hurts floor PSNR (21.46 to 18.37), the suppression loss removes the artifacts, and the BG floor loss restores floor quality (20.07). Dropping Splatfacto-W's alpha loss improves both metrics and visuals. Alpha and normal cues fail in complementary ways (texture-less surfaces vs. glass windows), so combining them gives the best node/edge validity (97.9/98.2 vs 92.4/89.2 for normal only).
method: Submap decomposition: agglomerative clustering of the camera trajectory into C submaps, each trained separately, with images from neighbours within distance δ added as overlap for consistent boundaries.

Hybrid floor segmentation: intersect EVF-SAM ('floor' text prompt) with a GeoWizard horizontal-surface normal mask, remove small connected components, sample K=3 points, and prompt SAM2 on the normal map to get the final floor mask.

Floor-aware Gaussian Splatting (Splatfacto-i): floor suppression loss (L1 of mask × accumulated alpha) and background floor loss (L1 between the SH background MLP render and the GT in the floor mask). The Splatfacto-W alpha loss is dropped, with λ_supp=λ_bg=1, λ_SSIM=0.2.
Camera pose embedding: an MLP maps the continuous camera position (no rotation) to the appearance embedding, replacing the per-camera index, for consistent novel-view appearance.

Mesh-free topological map: BFS from a starting viewpoint. At each node it renders spherical RGB/alpha views from the nearest submap and estimates normals with a foundation model. In each of 8 directions a ROI is traversable if mean alpha < 0.95 and upward normal > 0.85, and a new node is placed 2.5 m away. Node height is taken from the nearest trajectory point.
mLLM pairwise evaluation and R2R adaptation: mLLMs judge rendering quality on 375 image pairs; GPT-4o generates R2R instructions for paths in the built environment to test VLN agents.

setting.backbone: Per-submap 3D Gaussian Splatting (Splatfacto-i, trained per scene) + EVF-SAM, GeoWizard, SAM2 (frozen); R2R agents VLN-BERT (trained) and MapGPT (GPT-4o / GPT-5, frozen)
setting.training_data: Per-scene optimization on the COEX real-world indoor image sequence (~6,000 m², LiDAR-initialized, 15 submaps); VLN-BERT trained on generated R2R-style data; foundation models zero-shot
setting.observation: Monocular RGB image sequences with camera poses (spherical views rendered at graph nodes)
setting.action_space: Discrete topological graph viewpoints (8 directions, 2.5 m step)
setting.simulator: NVSim (own 3DGS-based simulator built on the COEX dataset)
setting.privileged: GT camera poses and LiDAR point clouds for initialization; OctoMap from LiDAR only as evaluation ground truth

numbers.extra: 10 submaps; GPT-4o generated instructions; baseline agent evaluated in the authors' NVSim environment

numbers_note: No standard benchmark numbers; the R2R results are on the authors' own generated COEX environment. Reconstruction PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS are in Tables 2 and 3 (with-floor PSNR 20.217, SSIM 0.824, LPIPS 0.399; without-floor PSNR 23.760, SSIM 0.883, LPIPS 0.234).
results: Splatfacto-i gives marginal reconstruction gains on non-floor regions (PSNR 23.760 vs 23.718 for Splatfacto-w) and is clearly preferred by mLLM judges (e.g. 93% win vs Splatfacto-w with GPT-5). Its alpha+normal traversability check gives 97.9% valid nodes and 98.2% valid edges. The generated environment supports R2R: VLN-BERT reaches SR 17.84 and MapGPT-GPT5 reaches 17.5, showing the task is harder than standard R2R.
limitations: Static scene only; the floor is modelled as low-frequency texture, so its detail and 3D height come from trajectory data, and the model gives no real geometry for collision.
Evaluated on a single environment (COEX); R2R instructions are LLM-generated with no human verification, and few agents were tested.
With-floor PSNR is lower than Splatfacto-W (20.217 vs 21.460); traversability relies on threshold heuristics and foundation-model normals, which fail on glass and texture-less surfaces.
